card.name: Be-verbs after a drug name
card.fires_on: Forms of "be" (be, is, are) or an adverb like "potentially" or "highly" right after a drug name or drug class as the subject. The next word is a property such as teratogenic, dialyzable, or contraindicated.

modes.label: "to be" after shown
modes.description: The word "be" follows a drug name and "shown to" or "known to", before a property.
modes.example: Salicylic acid has been shown to<< be>> teratogenic in rats and monkeys.

modes.label: is/are after drug subject
modes.description: "is" or "are" directly follows a drug or drug class, before a property or state.
modes.example: Hydroxyzine<< is>> contraindicated for patients who have

modes.label: Adverb before property
modes.description: An adverb after "is" comes before a drug property word.
modes.example: As with other aminoglycosides, gentamicin sulfate is<< potentially>> nephrotoxic.

card.plain: It marks the spot where a sentence about a drug is about to state a property of that drug, such as teratogenic or protein bound.
